newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says Israeli plan for Golan a threat.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israeli plan for Golan a threat.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper on Saturday blasted Israel's prime minister for approving a request by a state-owned company to drill for oil on the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Tishreen newspaper said the decision of Benjamin Netanyahu, reported on Friday in an Israeli newspaper, was a "blunt threat" to peace in the Middle East.
"There is no doubt that the government of Netanyahu deliberately works to destroy the remaining of the faint hopes for peace," it said.

The report in Israel's Haaretz newspaper had added that the actual drilling could be held up indefinitely -- despite Netanyahu's approval in principle -- by a recent decision to privatise the National Oil Company. Legal reviews of the request have still to be completed, the daily said.
Nearly five years of sporadic peace talks between Israel and Syria have long stalled over the strategic heights.

Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal. Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May elections, was ready to make at least a partial withdrawal for full peace and normal ties with Syria.
Netanyahu rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace.
